verdicts.reason: A separates the can from its circle: the can sits at the far right beside the body copy and the empty green circle floats alone on the left, so the hero image is broken. Its badges also collide ('BACK BYDEMAND' is missing a space) and the SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline. B at least keeps the can near the circle, but it doesn't sit inside it. B shares the cramped right-edge body copy, the same badge-sized CTA and the 'BYDEMAND' typo.

A layers the can over the circle, which keeps the original's product-in-circle motif, and its headline is bigger, which gives a stronger hierarchy. Its pills are still jammed together, the CTA is no bigger than the badges, and the tiny body copy is crowded against the right edge. B leaves the circle empty with the can floating in the gap. B also has the 'BACK BYDEMAND' spacing error, the same cramped right-edge copy, and a brand that reads below the headline.

These two are nearly identical: in both, the can is detached from the empty circle, the brand sits under the headline, the CTA is no bigger than the badges, and tiny body copy is stuck in the top-right corner. B fixes the 'BACK BY DEMAND' spacing and wraps the body copy a little more comfortably. A keeps the 'BYDEMAND' typo and its pills are more crowded.

A has the usual faults: the can is detached from the empty circle, the 'BYDEMAND' typo is there, and tiny body copy is wedged against the right edge, cut off from the text block. B pulls the body copy into the main text column, which groups and orders the content better. However, that line is now very small and hard to read, and the right third of the banner is dead space. The circle is still empty and the CTA still has no more weight than the badges.
